title: 11th Word: Introduction to the Parable and the Sultan's Purpose

questions.question: What does the passage invite the reader to understand by thinking about a short comparison?
questions.answer: It invites the reader to understand the purpose of the world, why human beings were created, and the mystery of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the comparison, what kind of person is introduced first?
questions.answer: A king with great wealth, knowledge, skills, and learning.

questions.question: What kinds of treasures did the king have?
questions.answer: He had many valuable treasures, including precious stones and other hidden wonderful riches.

questions.question: Besides wealth, what other strengths did the king have?
questions.answer: He had masterful skills in unusual arts, wide knowledge of amazing sciences, and deep learning.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a person who has beauty and perfection naturally want?
questions.answer: Such a person wants to see those qualities and also show them.

questions.question: What did the king want to establish in order to make his qualities known?
questions.answer: He wanted to set up an exhibition with displays.

questions.question: What four things did the king want people to notice through that exhibition?
questions.answer: He wanted them to see the greatness of his rule, his shining wealth, the wonders of his art, and the marvels of his knowledge.

questions.question: The passage says the king wanted to view his own beauty and perfection in two ways. What is the first way?
questions.answer: He wanted to behold them himself with his own aware and understanding sight.

questions.question: What is the second way the king wanted to view his beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: He wanted to see them through how others looked at them.

questions.question: What does this comparison suggest about why the king arranged the exhibition?
questions.answer: It suggests that the exhibition was made to reveal what he possessed and to let both he and others witness his excellence.

questions.question: What Qur’anic verses are placed at the beginning of the passage about?
questions.answer: They point to signs in creation such as the sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth, and the human self.

questions.question: After these verses, what does the speaker ask the reader to do?
questions.answer: The reader is asked to reflect on a brief comparison along with the speaker’s own self.

questions.question: Why is the king in the comparison described as having both visible and hidden treasures?
questions.answer: This shows that his riches were not limited to what people could easily see and that he possessed deeper wonders too.

questions.question: What do the king’s many arts and sciences tell us about him?
questions.answer: They show that he was highly capable, knowledgeable, and full of excellence.

questions.question: What desire moved the king to open a public display?
questions.answer: He wanted his beauty and perfection to become known and seen.

questions.question: Was the exhibition only for the people’s benefit, or did it also serve the king in some way? Explain.
questions.answer: It served both, because people would see his greatness, and he would also behold his qualities in two ways.

questions.question: What is one way the king wanted to witness his own excellence directly?
questions.answer: He wanted to see it himself with his own discerning sight.

questions.question: What is one way the king wanted to witness his own excellence indirectly?
questions.answer: He wanted to look at it as reflected in the awareness and view of others.

questions.question: What main idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: A being with great beauty and perfection wants those qualities to be manifested and observed.

questions.question: What three big topics does the passage say can be understood a little through the comparison?
questions.answer: The world’s purpose, the creation of human beings, and the mystery of the prayers.

questions.question: Who says this comparison is considered together with his own nafs?
questions.answer: The speaker says it is considered together with his own self.

questions.question: What does the king’s ownership of priceless jewels suggest about his condition?
questions.answer: It suggests he was extremely wealthy and possessed rare riches.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention hidden treasures as well as open ones?
questions.answer: To show that the king had deeper stores of wonder beyond what appeared on the surface.

questions.question: How is the king’s knowledge described?
questions.answer: It is described as broad, amazing, and spread across many branches of learning.

questions.question: What kind of arts did the king master?
questions.answer: He mastered remarkable and unusual arts.

questions.question: Why did the king want to arrange displays before people?
questions.answer: He wanted to make his rule, wealth, art, and knowledge visible.

questions.question: What are the two sides of the king’s wish to see his own perfection?
questions.answer: One side is seeing it himself, and the other is seeing it through others.

questions.question: What can we infer about the king’s exhibition from the words majesty, wealth, art, and knowledge?
questions.answer: We can infer that it was meant to reveal many forms of excellence, not just material riches.

questions.question: In this passage, is the king presented as lacking greatness or as already possessing it? How do you know?
questions.answer: He is presented as already possessing it, because the passage lists his treasures, skills, knowledge, and learning before describing the exhibition.

questions.question: What is the basic setup of the comparison in the passage?
questions.answer: A powerful king with great riches and knowledge wants to display his excellence.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the king’s learning besides his skills and wealth?
questions.answer: It says he had deep knowledge in many difficult areas of learning.

questions.question: What human tendency does the passage mention before explaining the king’s action?
questions.answer: It says that one who has beauty and perfection wants to see and show them.

questions.question: How does that tendency help explain the king’s decision?
questions.answer: It explains why he wanted to open an exhibition and place displays in it.

questions.question: What part of the king’s authority did he want people to notice?
questions.answer: He wanted them to notice the greatness and glory of his rule.

questions.question: What part of the king’s possessions did he want shown?
questions.answer: He wanted his shining and rich treasures to be seen.

questions.question: What part of the king’s abilities did he want displayed?
questions.answer: He wanted the wonders of his craftsmanship and the marvels of his knowledge to be displayed.

questions.question: Why does the passage divide the king’s goal into two respects?
questions.answer: To show that his aim involved both his own witnessing and the witnessing of others.

questions.question: Which comes first in the two respects: the king’s own seeing or the people’s seeing?
questions.answer: The king’s own seeing comes first.

questions.question: What does the opening section from the Qur’an mention before the comparison begins?
questions.answer: It mentions major signs in creation and the shaping of the human self.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the world’s purpose and human creation before giving the example?
questions.answer: They are described as something like a hidden puzzle or mystery to be understood.

questions.question: What was special about the king’s treasures besides their value?
questions.answer: Some were open and some were concealed, and all were described as wonderful.

questions.question: What personal qualities of the king are emphasized in addition to possessions?
questions.answer: His artistic skill, his broad knowledge, and his deep scholarship.

questions.question: What reason is given for why a possessor of beauty and perfection wants to display them?
questions.answer: Because such a possessor naturally wants to witness and show those qualities.

questions.question: What did the king hope people would see when he prepared his display?
questions.answer: He hoped they would see the greatness of his kingdom, his wealth, his art, and his knowledge.

questions.question: How many viewpoints did the king want for seeing his own beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: Two viewpoints.

questions.question: What is meant by the first viewpoint?
questions.answer: It means he wanted to behold those qualities directly himself.

questions.question: What is meant by the second viewpoint?
questions.answer: It means he wanted to observe those qualities through the gaze and recognition of others.

questions.question: What subjects does the passage connect together before giving the story of the king?
questions.answer: It connects the purpose of the world, the creation of mankind, and the meaning of the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: In the comparison, what shows that the king was not ordinary?
questions.answer: His many priceless treasures, hidden wonders, extraordinary arts, and vast learning show that he was not ordinary.

questions.question: Why is the king’s knowledge of many sciences important in the comparison?
questions.answer: It helps show that his greatness included wisdom and understanding, not just wealth.

questions.question: What does the passage say people with beauty and perfection want to do?
questions.answer: They want to see those qualities and make them known.

questions.question: How did the king plan to make his qualities visible to people?
questions.answer: He planned to open an exhibition and arrange displays in it.

questions.question: Name two things the king wanted people to notice through the exhibition.
questions.answer: He wanted them to notice his royal greatness and the wonders of his art.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the king beholding his beauty and perfection with his own discerning eye?
questions.answer: It means he wanted direct awareness of his own excellence.

questions.question: What does it mean that he also wanted to look through the view of others?
questions.answer: It means he wanted his excellence to be reflected in how others saw and recognized it.

questions.question: What relationship is shown between inner excellence and outward display in the passage?
questions.answer: Inner excellence leads to an outward display so that it can be known and witnessed.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the comparison as a whole?
questions.answer: It is to help the reader think about deeper truths by using the example of a king who reveals his greatness through what he displays.
